title: What fractions name the marks when a unit has eight parts?
description: A unit on the number line is cut into eight equal parts, and the marks from zero to one need fractions. The board finds the size of one part, names a mark by counting its parts and checks that all eight parts fill the unit. Keeko doubts the count of the third mark by including zero.
teaching_notes: One idea: the mark after some parts from zero is that many times one eighth. Watch for students who count zero as a part and name the third mark four eighths.

source: Now, a unit on the number line is divided into 8 equal parts
video_script.why: A learner names every mark of a unit cut into eight equal parts by counting the parts from zero.
video_script.substitution: the book's own number line with a unit cut into eight equal parts
video_script.anchor: the number line with the unit from 0 to 1 cut into eight equal parts
video_script.wrong_answer: the third mark is four eighths
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko counts zero as a mark of its own, so every mark gets a count one too big.
video_script.payoff_line: The marks are the eighths from one eighth to eight eighths

final_answer.spoken: one eighth, two eighths, up to eight eighths, which is one

video_script.fraction_reading: one eighth, two eighths, three eighths, four eighths, five eighths, six eighths, seven eighths, eight eighths
maths_rules: 1 unit cut into 8 equal parts: each part is 1/8 unit
the mark after n parts from 0 is n x 1/8 = n/8
check: 8 x 1/8 = 8/8 = 1, the end of the unit
video_script.design: One unit from zero to one cut into eight parts. Each mark is named by its count of parts, and Keeko's doubt counts zero as a part.

<bookmark mark='line'/>A unit on the number line is cut into eight equal parts.
<bookmark mark='marks'/>The marks from zero to one have no labels yet.
Which fractions name these marks?

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

narration: <bookmark mark='parts'/>Each of the eight equal parts of a unit is one eighth.
<bookmark mark='first'/>A mark is named by how many parts lie between zero and that mark.

beats.on_screen: Given: the unit from 0 to 1 is cut into 8 equal parts
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the unit from zero to one is cut into eight equal parts.

beats.on_screen: To find: the fraction for each mark from 0 to 1
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the fraction for each mark from zero to one.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: 1 unit into 8 equal parts, each part = 1/8

marks.size: one part is lit and labelled 1/8

narration: <bookmark mark='size'/>Step one, find the size of each part. One unit cut into eight equal parts gives one eighth each.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: mark after n parts = n x 1/8 = n/8; third mark = 3 x 1/8; fifth mark = 5 x 1/8

marks.rule: the rule for a mark is written under the line

marks.fifth: the fifth mark is lit with its five parts shaded

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step two, a mark that is some parts from zero is that number times one eighth.
<bookmark mark='third'/>The third mark is three times one eighth.
<bookmark mark='fifth'/>The fifth mark is five times one eighth.

beats.on_screen: Check: all 8 parts fill the unit from 0 to 1

marks.check: all eight parts are shaded and reach the mark 1

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>To check, all eight parts together fill the unit, so the last mark must be at one.

marks.ans: the first four marks are labelled
marks.rest: the last four marks are labelled
marks.whole: the last label is written as equal to 1

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The marks are the eighths from one eighth to eight eighths.
They are one eighth, two eighths, three eighths and four eighths.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Then come five eighths, six eighths, seven eighths and eight eighths.
<bookmark mark='whole'/>Eight eighths is the whole unit, which is one.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the number line
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a bubble says the third mark is 4/8 because zero is counted too; the parts up to the third mark are shaded and only three fit; the bubble is struck out

marks.doubt: the bubble with the wrong idea appears
marks.shade: the parts from 0 to the third mark are shaded and counted
marks.fix: the bubble is struck out and the mark is relabelled 3/8

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the third mark is four eighths, because zero is counted too.
<bookmark mark='shade'/>Shade the parts from zero up to the third mark. Only three parts fit.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Zero is where we start, so we count the parts, not the marks.
